source: Curated Stage-1 inventory derived by the methodology in docs/content-bank-strategy.md (value-vs-decomposition-cost). Expands the v0 seed (Gleitman & Rozin Table 1) into a story-capable set. See content/curation-v1.md for the full rationale.
notes: 53 elements (27 picturable pictograph anchors that head rhyme families + a lean core of function/suffix glyphs) generating 76 words, including plural -s and -ing morphology. Symbol tiers, IPA and Dolch tiers are best-effort. Rebus picture-words are flagged in notes (i = eye, before = bee+for, window = wind+o).

elements.notes: Object 'can' doubles as auxiliary verb (rebus seed); -an with man.
Pictured as a window; window = wind+o.
Pictured as an eye (eye = I rebus); the pronoun 'I'.
Most frequent English word; irregular 'th' kept whole for now.
Meaningless -er suffix; marks semantic vs phonological unit (sunnier).
Plural marker; pup+s = pups, can+s = canz (morphophonemic, Stage 3).
-ing suffix; go+ing = going; rhymes with ring.
Early compound fuel (catfish, starfish); introduces sh.
Joins the -ee family (bee, key, see); compound fuel (treehouse).

words.inclusion_rationale: Picturable object that doubles as the auxiliary verb — the rebus seed.
Core pronoun, picturable as an eye (rebus).
The most frequent word; taught as a whole sight syllable.
Weather word; reuses window glyph for its sound.
Picturable object built transparently from wind+o.
Adds the meaningless -er syllable on a known blend (Stage-3 bridge).
Held-out test blend; pure phonological blend pen+sill.
Held-out three-syllable test blend reusing sill.
Plural; the paper's own example (pup + s).
Early pictograph compound: sun+hat blendable from Unit 1.
Pictograph compound: pig+pen — the rebus insight with two pictures.
